# Taxonomy and decision space

**Problem → Decision → Alternatives → Trade-offs → Evaluation → Research.**
These fourteen domains are knowledge responsibilities, not fourteen mandatory pipeline stages. Domains 01–09 describe core ER decisions; 10–12 own research/evaluation; 13–14 own system-level constraints. Scoring and clustering are not interchangeable terms. Related-to edges do not establish same-as membership.

| Domain | Responsibility | Main question |
|---|---|---|
| [01](domains/01-problem-identity.md) | Problem Formulation & Identity Semantics | What does one entity mean, and what output constitutes a correct resolution? |
| [02](domains/02-architecture-orchestration.md) | Pipeline Architecture & Orchestration | How should components interact, route work and revise decisions? |
| [03](domains/03-data-integration.md) | Data Understanding & Integration | Which observations are semantically comparable and sufficiently reliable to use? |
| [04](domains/04-normalization-enrichment.md) | Normalization & Enrichment | Which transformations make values comparable without erasing identity evidence? |
| [05](domains/05-candidate-retrieval.md) | Candidate Generation & Retrieval | Which pairs merit scoring under a candidate budget, and which true matches could be missed? |
| [06](domains/06-comparison-evidence.md) | Comparison Features & Evidence Engineering | What similarities, contradictions and contextual observations should a scorer see? |
| [07](domains/07-matching-scoring.md) | Matching & Scoring | How should evidence be aggregated into a score whose interpretation is clear? |
| [08](domains/08-decision-resolution.md) | Decision Policies & Entity Resolution | When should a score trigger a link, abstention, assignment or entity-membership change? |
| [09](domains/09-master-maintenance.md) | Master Entity Construction & Maintenance | How should resolved entities be represented, updated and corrected without hiding evidence? |
| [10](domains/10-ground-truth.md) | Ground Truth & Labeling | What labeled evidence supports training, evaluation and diagnosis for the actual target population? |
| [11](domains/11-evaluation-diagnostics.md) | Evaluation & Diagnostics | Which measurements reveal local quality, final identity quality and the cost of errors? |
| [12](domains/12-experimentation.md) | Experimentation & Research Methods | Which controlled test would distinguish mechanisms and reduce decision uncertainty? |
| [13](domains/13-scalability-execution.md) | Scalability & Execution | How can a logically valid ER design fit resource and update constraints without concealing quality loss? |
| [14](domains/14-governance-monitoring.md) | Explainability, Governance & Monitoring | How can users understand, audit, correct and monitor identity decisions safely? |

## Boundaries that prevent duplicate knowledge
- Source profiling: **03**; quality-aware evidence: **06**; learned weighting: **07**.
- Single-record transformations: **04**; pair comparisons: **06**.
- Retrieval logic: **05**; physical execution/index maintenance: **13**.
- Score interpretation/calibration: **07**; score-dependent actions and membership: **08**; consumer entity construction: **09**.
- Label construction: **10**; measurements: **11**; experiment procedures: **12**.
- Lifecycle/topology: **02** with resource details in **13** and identity-state consequences in **09**.

## Cross-cutting dependencies
Normalization changes retrieval keys and evidence. Retrieval changes the score/calibration population. Scoring quality does not guarantee entity-quality improvement. Membership decisions affect master attributes and future graph features, which can feed errors back into matching. Privacy constraints can remove otherwise available evidence. Labeling, monitoring and experiments must evaluate these interactions rather than attributing all errors to a matcher.

See [independent architecture dimensions](architecture-dimensions.md), [conceptual contracts](module-contracts.md), [catalog](../CATALOG.md), and [reconciliation](../guides/design-reconciliation.md). Pilot method coverage is deliberately narrower than this taxonomy; the [expansion plan](../guides/expansion-plan.md) records the gap.

# 01 — Problem Formulation & Identity Semantics

**Design question:** What does one entity mean, and what output constitutes a correct resolution?

## Decisions and coverage
- Deduplication within a source; cross-source linkage; multi-source identity resolution. Define the eligible record-pair universe, not just the observed candidate pool.
- Entity types and identity semantics: a person is not a household; an organization may be a legal entity, branch, or operating group. Same-as identity and related-to relationships require different labels.
- One-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many constraints depend on whether source rows are unique entities or repeated observations. Temporal identity specifies how name changes, identifier reuse and organizational succession are treated.
- Pairwise links, entity memberships and uncertain identity alternatives are distinct outputs. Specify asymmetric false-merge/missed-match costs and the unit of harm.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Strict identity with validated identifiers; source-scoped identities; time-indexed identity definitions.
- Independent scored links; constrained assignment with an unmatched option; membership partitions; uncertainty-preserving links.

## Ownership and limitations
Incremental is a lifecycle choice, collective is an inference strategy, and neither changes the meaning of identity by itself.

This is a domain map, not complete L2 method coverage. Unexpanded families are retained for [expansion review](../../guides/expansion-plan.md); mature names are not automatic recommendations.

# 02 — Pipeline Architecture & Orchestration

**Design question:** How should components interact, route work and revise decisions?

## Decisions and coverage
- Linear, cascaded/multi-stage, parallel/multi-branch and iterative/collective topologies.
- Single matcher, hybrid rules/statistics/ML and ensembles are composition choices, not unique topologies.
- Adaptive compute routing and human-in-the-loop workflows need escalation, review-capacity and correction contracts.
- Batch, incremental and streaming orchestration share logical matching components but differ in state, timing and replay requirements. Intermediate artifacts need explicit versioned contracts.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Linear modular baseline; recall-oriented multi-pass; precision-first adaptive cascade.
- Parallel multi-model fusion; collective/consistency-aware resolution; incremental/continuous processing.

# 09 — Master Entity Construction & Maintenance

**Design question:** How should resolved entities be represented, updated and corrected without hiding evidence?

## Decisions and coverage
- Golden records, linked-record/virtual entities and hybrid master representations offer different consumer simplicity and provenance visibility.
- Attribute survivorship can use source precedence, recency, field confidence or multiple values; observation time is not necessarily validity time.
- Stable entity identifiers, temporal histories and field/source/decision lineage must survive incremental membership maintenance.
- Reversible merges and entity splits need ID redirection/versioning and downstream correction semantics. Identity relationships must remain distinct from other relationships. Entity confidence cannot be inferred by multiplying dependent edge scores.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Membership-preserving virtual entities with a derived canonical view; a documented golden-record policy.
- Versioned entities, uncertainty-preserving attribute alternatives and explicit merge/split histories.

## Ownership and limitations
08 decides membership. This domain decides representation and identity-maintenance consequences; audit/control permissions remain in 14.

# AR-05 — Collective/Consistency-Aware Resolution

## Philosophy and four dimensions

Independent plausible pairs may be incompatible with the requested identity output. Couple decisions only when the task warrants it. Primary work demonstrates adaptive query-time relational collective resolution in publication databases; it does not validate every constrained resolver or establish universal gains.[10] This broader archetype is Atlas synthesis.

- **Topology:** scored candidates followed by joint resolution; optionally iterative evidence/resolution feedback. A one-shot assignment is also compatible.
- **Scoring paradigm:** deterministic, additive, probabilistic, supervised, neural, or hybrid pair/relational evidence.
- **Resolution:** assignment, constrained membership, or relational collective inference, explicitly distinguished below.
- **Lifecycle:** batch or maintained incrementally. Federated privacy/access restrictions separately constrain relational visibility and feasible joint computation.

## Pipeline and modules

`Eligible candidates → comparison/scoring → constraints and optional relationships → joint resolver → dispositions/membership → optional evidence refresh`.

Required modules are identity/cardinality specification, candidates and evidence, declared score/objective semantics, a resolver, and decision provenance. Relational data and iterative inference are optional unless the selected configuration depends on them. Constraint validation and infeasibility handling are required whenever constraints are imposed. Optional modules include review, uncertainty analysis, entity construction, and rollback support.

## Resolution alternatives and rationale

1. **One-to-one assignment:** eligible cross-source links compete because each observation may be assigned at most once. Include explicit unmatched options and their costs; forcing a complete matching can create false links. This is not unrestricted duplicate clustering.
2. **Constrained clustering:** decide memberships with must-link/cannot-link or cardinality conditions. Constraints need scope and temporal meaning. Simple transitive closure can overmerge through one erroneous bridge; rejecting bridges or optimizing memberships are different policies.
3. **Relational collective inference:** linked references or entities influence one another's identity hypotheses. Relationship types must remain distinct from same-as identity. Co-occurrence-based joint resolution is a concrete primary-literature example.[10] Merely sharing an address or collaborator is not an identity rule.

A graph can represent evidence or dependencies, but it is not required for assignment or constrained membership. Hard constraints encode admissibility; soft penalties encode preferences. Neither should be silently treated as observed truth.

## Conceptual input/output contracts

Use the [module contracts](../taxonomy/module-contracts.md).

- **Evidence input:** versioned candidate pairs and [comparison states](../solutions/comparison-features/evidence-states.md). **Output:** scores with declared scale, model version, provenance, and optional typed relationship observations.
- **Constraint input:** source/cardinality rules, temporal scope, and adjudicated conditions. **Output:** versioned admissibility rules or penalties with justification and conflict diagnostics.
- **Resolver input:** candidate scores, constraints, unmatched/singleton options, and optional relationship evidence. **Output:** selected assignments or memberships, unresolved cases, constraint violations/infeasibility, and decision explanations.
- **Iteration input:** provisional memberships and original evidence. **Output:** revised evidence/objective values and a versioned resolution proposal; retain stopping criteria and feedback lineage.

Illustratively, two plausible matches competing for one target require a choice or unmatched outcome, not two independent acceptances. Output confidence must distinguish pair certainty from the stability of that joint choice.

## Assumptions and scorer compatibility

Use when one-to-one cardinality is genuinely warranted, duplicate groups need membership consistency, or relationships supply relevant identity information. Reject inappropriate one-to-one assumptions when a source legitimately repeats the same entity. Relational coverage and meanings may differ across sources.

[Additive scoring](../solutions/matching-scoring/additive-soft-matching.md), [Fellegi–Sunter](../solutions/matching-scoring/fellegi-sunter.md), or [logistic regression](../solutions/matching-scoring/logistic-regression.md) can supply evidence, but objective-compatible utilities must be specified; optimizing arbitrary score sums is not automatically optimal expected loss. Deterministic constraints need no training labels, yet adjudication is needed to assess their correctness. Learned relational components require leakage-safe labels; entity and connected-context separation may be necessary beyond random pair splits.

## Mechanism, costs, and failures

The proposed advantage is excluding incompatible local decisions or borrowing informative context. Benefits require correct constraints and useful context. False constraints force systematic errors; relational feedback can amplify a mistaken seed. Candidate omissions still restrict feasible true resolutions.

Assignment, constrained clustering, and relational iteration have different costs; no single complexity claim covers them. Large ambiguous groups increase memory and optimization burden. Approximation, stopping rules, partition boundaries, and update order can affect outcomes. Repeatedly counting context derived from the same provisional memberships can create unsupported certainty.

## Interactions, evaluation, and research

[AR-06](incremental-continuous.md) must revisit dependent competitors and relationships, not only changed records. Multi-pass retrieval and ensembles can feed this resolver if score meanings and candidate scope remain explicit.

Evaluate [pair calibration](../evaluation/pairwise-calibration.md) separately from [entity quality](../evaluation/entity-resolution-quality.md), assignment accuracy, unmatched quality, constraint errors, and runtime. Compare independent pair decisions with joint resolution on identical scored candidates. Variations include soft constraints and reviewed conflict sets. Research should ablate constraints and relationships separately, inject erroneous conditions, and test sensitivity to missing context. No universal advantage is claimed.

## Sources

[10] https://cdn.aaai.org/AAAI/2007/AAAI07-255.pdf — Online Collective Entity Resolution

# Conceptual module contracts

These contracts describe knowledge-level artifacts, not APIs, code classes, a mandatory technology stack, or an executable pipeline. Carry raw observation provenance and component versions forward. A deployment may combine modules physically without erasing their responsibilities.

| Module | Input | Output | Invariant / question to settle |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intake/integration | Source observations, schemas, identifier namespaces and observation/validity times | Comparable typed observations plus raw references, validity/quality flags and mapping versions | Same named field need not mean same attribute; no silent conflict overwrites |
| Normalization/enrichment | Typed observations and locale/source context | Raw plus normalized/parsed/variant representations, transformation provenance and uncertainty | Lossy transformation must not replace the only evidence copy |
| Candidate generation | Representations, eligible pair definition, retrieval/index versions and budgets | Unique record pairs, source pairs, pass/routing provenance, retrieval reasons, omissions/caps | Canonical pair identity; absent candidate is unknown, not a known non-match |
| Comparison | Candidate pair and observation histories | Evidence vector, missing/invalid/conflict masks, source/time context, dependency groups, feature version | Separate absence from reliable contradiction; reveal shared provenance |
| Scoring | Versioned evidence and applicable trained/estimated/manual model | Score, score semantics, contributions, model version and conditioning population | A raw additive sum or LR is not automatically a calibrated posterior |
| Calibration | Scores plus independent representative calibration reference | Population-specific probability mapping and validity conditions | Changed retrieval/routing/source mix can invalidate it |
| Decision policy | Scores/probabilities, loss/cardinality assumptions and review budget | Link/non-link/abstain disposition, rationale and policy version | Pairwise policy does not by itself enforce globally consistent membership |
| Joint resolution (optional) | Scored pairs, known constraints and unresolved alternatives | Assignments/partition or uncertainty-preserving memberships, decision trace, conflicts | Unscored edge is not a cannot-link; unmatched options must exist when allowed |
| Entity construction | Membership decisions and original observations | Golden/virtual/hybrid representation, field lineage, stable/versioned entity identity | Membership truth and chosen consumer value are different questions |
| Review/correction | Evidence traces and uncertain or audited decisions | Adjudicated label, correction authorization, membership/attribute change history | Model predictions cannot automatically become independent gold labels |
| Incremental maintenance | New/changed/deleted observations, state/version dependencies | Recomputed affected artifacts, ID redirections, reversible merge/split events | Dependency closure can extend beyond the changed record; distinguish event time and processing time |

## Composition and failure containment
- A cascade records terminal and escalated decisions plus routing versions; evaluate early exits separately, not just the remaining hard cases.
- A parallel composition keeps missing branch outputs distinct from negative branch evidence; fusion must use comparable scales or a justified learned map.
- An iterative composition records the context snapshot and iteration producing a feature; known labels and predicted memberships must not be confused.
- A budgeted retriever declares whether truncation/splitting sacrifices coverage. Index build and update costs belong in total compute accounting.
- Reversible entity changes require restoring membership/lineage and notifying downstream consumers; simply deleting a link does not necessarily reverse its transitive effects.

See [dimensions](architecture-dimensions.md), [taxonomy ownership](overview.md), and the [catalog](../CATALOG.md) for actual alternatives. Contracts are Atlas design synthesis; they are not externally benchmarked requirements.

# 03 — Data Understanding & Integration

**Design question:** Which observations are semantically comparable and sufficiently reliable to use?

## Decisions and coverage
- Profile completeness, uniqueness, value distributions, validity, duplicates and changing source coverage; do not infer reliability solely from agreement with current ER predictions.
- Align schemas manually, with rules or learned suggestions; distinguish similarly named fields with different semantics. Canonical, flexible and hybrid representations trade comparison simplicity against retained source detail.
- Identifier semantics require namespaces, issuance authority, formatting rules, reuse and validity periods. Source and attribute reliability are not a single universal source ranking.
- Retain provenance, conflicting observations, temporal data histories and schema versions. Cross-source compatibility includes units, calendars, geography and observation granularity.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Strict canonical schema; flexible attributes; canonical core plus source extensions.
- Preserve all observations; deferred reconciliation; documented source precedence for a consumer view.

## Ownership and limitations
Source profiling is owned here. Quality-derived pair features are 06; learned weighting is 07; selecting master attributes is 09.

Simple baseline and materially different alternatives:
1.  **Simple Baseline:** The current production pipeline.
    *   Mechanism: Exact equality on registration. Accumulates permanent unions (merges). Replaces previous name/address with latest. Ignores deletions.

2.  **Materially Different Alternative: Collective/Consistency-Aware Resolution with Temporal and Relational Semantics.**
    *   Mechanism: Instead of simple exact matching, this approach couples resolution decisions based on identity semantics, cardinality constraints, and relational dependencies. It explicitly distinguishes between "one-to-one assignment," "constrained clustering," and "relational collective inference" (AR-05). It emphasizes handling temporal identity, identifier reuse, and explicit representation of "related-to" relationships distinct from "same-as" (Domain 01). It requires maintaining versioned entities and explicit merge/split histories (Domain 09) and preserving provenance (Domain 03).
    *   Prerequisites: Clear definition of "legal entity continuity," "business continuity," and authoritative namespaces/validity intervals (currently unknown). Requires richer comparison features that include temporal attributes. Needs a mechanism to adjudicate and encode constraints.
    *   Tradeoffs: Increased complexity in design, implementation, and maintenance. Requires more sophisticated data modeling and potentially higher computational resources.
    *   Costs: Higher upfront development cost; potential for incorrect constraints to propagate errors; increased operational complexity.
    *   Failure modes: Incorrectly defined constraints can force systematic errors (AR-05). Over-complexity can hinder auditability. Insufficiently rich data can still lead to misidentification.

Candidate configurations:
1.  **Topology:** A "Linear/Modular Baseline" (AR-01 in L0) as a conceptual framework, but with "Collective/Consistency-Aware Resolution" (AR-05) integrated as the decision module. This implies "scored candidates followed by joint resolution" (AR-05). The system must allow for "iterative evidence/resolution feedback" (AR-05) to refine entity hypotheses.
2.  **Scoring:** Pairwise scoring (e.g., Fellegi-Sunter, Logistic Regression mentioned in L0 and compatible with AR-05) should generate scores for potential "same-as" links. Critically, comparison features (Domain 06, L0) must incorporate temporal aspects, such as date ranges of names/addresses and registration validity. AR-05 notes that objective-compatible utilities must be specified, as "optimizing arbitrary score sums is not automatically optimal expected loss."
3.  **Resolution:** Employ "Constrained clustering" or "One-to-one assignment" (AR-05) to prevent over-merging and handle identifier reuse like Q-41. This must include "explicit unmatched options" (AR-05) to avoid forcing incorrect matches. For successorship, "Relational collective inference" (AR-05) can be used, ensuring "relationship types must remain distinct from same-as identity." "Membership-preserving virtual entities" with "versioned entities, uncertainty-preserving attribute alternatives and explicit merge/split histories" (Domain 09) are essential for output.
4.  **Lifecycle:** "Incremental/Continuous Entity Resolution" (AR-06, a complement to AR-05) is implied by the need for "replay and stable references" and handling corrections. "Dependency closure can extend beyond the changed record" (module contracts) meaning changes to one entity might affect related entities.
5.  **Module Contracts:**
    *   **Intake/Integration:** Must preserve "source observations, schemas, identifier namespaces and observation/validity times" and "raw references, validity/quality flags" (module contracts).
    *   **Comparison:** Must produce an "Evidence vector, missing/invalid/conflict masks, source/time context, dependency groups" (module contracts).
    *   **Joint Resolution:** Input "Scored pairs, known constraints and unresolved alternatives," output "Assignments/partition or uncertainty-preserving memberships, decision trace, conflicts" (module contracts). This includes ensuring "unmatched options must exist when allowed" and "unscored edge is not a cannot-link" (module contracts).
    *   **Entity Construction:** "Golden/virtual/hybrid representation, field lineage, stable/versioned entity identity" (module contracts) to maintain historical views and support corrections.
    *   **Incremental Maintenance:** "Recomputed affected artifacts, ID redirections, reversible merge/split events" (module contracts).

Risks, constraints and safeguards:
1.  **Risks:**
    *   **Over-merging/Under-merging:** Incorrectly defined identity semantics or constraints can lead to organizations being incorrectly merged or split. The current pipeline exemplifies over-merging.
    *   **Loss of Temporal Context:** Failure to properly version records or handle validity intervals can obscure organizational histories.
    *   **Complexity Overload:** Implementing advanced collective resolution and temporal entity management can introduce significant complexity, making the system harder to understand, debug, and maintain.
    *   **Data Quality Dependence:** The accuracy of the system will heavily depend on the quality and completeness of event dates and observation dates, which are noted to be sometimes lacking in supplier rows.
    *   **Incorrect Constraint Specification:** As AR-05 warns, "False constraints force systematic errors."

2.  **Constraints:**
    *   Identity continuity across ordinary address/name changes is useful.
    *   Successorship and acquisition relationships must remain navigable without assuming sameness.
    *   Corrections must support replay and stable references.
    *   Requires distinguishing legal entity from business continuity (currently unknown).
    *   Requires authoritative namespaces, validity intervals, reuse, and event dates (currently unknown).

3.  **Safeguards:**
    *   **Explicit Identity Semantics:** Clearly define "what one entity means" (Domain 01) including temporal aspects, and formally document these.
    *   **Versioned Entities & Histories:** Implement "versioned entities, uncertainty-preserving attribute alternatives and explicit merge/split histories" (Domain 09) to preserve historical context and enable replay.
    *   **Provenance Retention:** "Retain provenance, conflicting observations, temporal data histories" (Domain 03) to audit decisions.
    *   **Granular Decision Resolution:** Use "Collective/Consistency-Aware Resolution" (AR-05) with careful constraint definition and "unmatched options" to avoid forced merges.
    *   **Human-in-the-Loop:** Design for review and correction workflows for ambiguous or high-risk cases.
    *   **Phased Implementation:** Start with a baseline, then progressively introduce more complex features, especially for collective resolution and temporal management, evaluating at each step.

Proposed falsifiable experiment:
1.  **Objective:** Demonstrate that the proposed design (Collective/Consistency-Aware Resolution with Temporal Semantics and Versioned Entities) can correctly distinguish legal entity changes, identifier reuse, and successorships, preserving historical accuracy and stable references, significantly outperforming the current "exact registration equality" baseline.
2.  **Comparator:**
    *   **Baseline:** The current production pipeline's output (entities formed by exact registration equality, latest name/address replacement, ignored deletions).
    *   **Proposed:** The output of the new ER design (using collective resolution, temporal features, and versioned entities).
3.  **Controls:**
    *   **Data Split:** Use a held-out dataset of annual filings and supplier records, ensuring a representative sample of historical events, including known Q-41 type scenarios, successorships, and routine name/address changes.
    *   **Consistent Input:** Both the baseline and proposed system will process the identical input data.
4.  **Independent Labels/Splits:**
    *   **Ground Truth Creation:** Manual annotation (or expert judgment) on a subset of the held-out data to establish ground truth for:
        *   True legal entity continuity (e.g., same entity despite name/address change).
        *   True entity splits (e.g., a company divests a subsidiary that becomes a new legal entity).
        *   True entity merges/acquisitions (e.g., Company A acquires Company B, and B ceases to exist as a separate legal entity, or continues as a related but distinct entity).
        *   True identifier reuse events (like Q-41, where the registration number refers to distinct legal entities at different times).
        *   True "related-to" relationships (e.g., predecessor/successor) that are not "same-as."
    *   **Label Granularity:** Labels must distinguish between "same legal entity at time T," "related entity at time T," and "distinct entity at time T."
5.  **Candidate and Final-Entity Metrics:**
    *   **Final Entity Metrics (Primary):**
        *   **Entity Precision/Recall:** Adapted for temporal entities and relationships. E.g., how many pairs identified as "same legal entity at time T" are actually "same," and how many true "same legal entity at time T" pairs were found.
        *   **Relationship Accuracy:** For "related-to" links (successorship, acquisition), measure precision and recall.
        *   **Temporal Consistency:** Metrics for correctly identifying periods of validity for names, addresses, and registrations.
        *   **Split/Merge Accuracy:** Quantify correct identification of entity splits and merges based on ground truth.
        *   **Stable Reference Accuracy:** Evaluate the stability and correctness of entity IDs over time, especially after "corrections" or "mergers."
    *   **Candidate Metrics (Secondary):** "Candidate recall and retrieval efficiency" (EVAL-11-001 in L0) to ensure the candidate generation stage is not pre-emptively losing true matches, especially across temporal boundaries or different blocking keys.
6.  **Slices:** Evaluate metrics across different challenging slices:
    *   Cases involving identifier reuse (e.g., Q-41).
    *   Cases with known successorship/acquisition events.
    *   Entities undergoing frequent name/address changes.
    *   Supplier records lacking explicit event/observation dates.
7.  **Uncertainty and Practical Guardrails:**
    *   Acknowledge the inherent difficulty and cost of creating comprehensive historical ground truth for organizational identity.
    *   Establish clear definitions for "legal entity continuity" vs. "business continuity" before labeling.
    *   Define a threshold for "good enough" performance for the more complex scenarios (e.g., 90% accuracy on Q-41 type events).
    *   If manual labeling is extensive, provide estimated labeling cost and time.

Next decisions for positive, negative and inconclusive evidence:
1.  **Positive Evidence:** If the experiment demonstrates a statistically significant improvement in temporal identity resolution, correct handling of identifier reuse, and accurate representation of successorship relationships (especially against the current pipeline's known failure modes), and the error rates for complex scenarios (e.g., Q-41) are within acceptable bounds, then:
    *   **Decision:** Proceed with a pilot implementation of the proposed ER architecture on a larger, controlled dataset.
    *   **Next Step:** Refine the detailed design for specific comparison features and constraint enforcement, focusing on the most impactful gains observed.
2.  **Negative Evidence:** If the proposed solution performs worse than or not materially better than the baseline in critical areas (e.g., still incorrectly merges Q-41, fails to preserve successorship), or introduces unacceptable new failure modes (e.g., excessive over-splitting), then:
    *   **Decision:** Re-evaluate the core assumptions and mechanisms of the proposed design.
    *   **Next Step:** Analyze the specific failure types in detail (e.g., which constraints failed, where did temporal features not provide enough signal). Consider simplifying the collective resolution strategy or re-visiting the definition of identity semantics and ground truth.
3.  **Inconclusive Evidence:** If the experiment results are ambiguous, or show mixed performance with some gains but also new issues, or if the confidence intervals are too wide to draw a clear conclusion, then:
    *   **Decision:** Do not proceed with full implementation; conduct further targeted experimentation.
    *   **Next Step:** Refine the experiment design, focusing on the most ambiguous slices of data or the specific mechanisms showing mixed results. This may involve gathering more granular ground truth, adjusting parameters, or isolating specific components for testing (e.g., testing only the temporal comparison features' impact).

rubric.cap_rule: Evaluator supplies raw scores and evidenced failure IDs. Harness computes each effective score as min(raw_score, all triggered caps for that dimension). Others unchanged. No aggregate and no overall pass claim. Failed/unexecuted runs have no scores.

alternative_quality.0: One unjustified option or cosmetic variants only.
alternative_quality.1: Names distinct alternatives without meaningful comparator/selection logic.
alternative_quality.2: Credible simple baseline and different plausible alternative with tradeoffs.
alternative_quality.3: Compares mechanisms, prerequisites, costs and exclusions; justifies when complexity is or is not warranted.

efficiency.0: Violates a hard run budget or unusable final output.
efficiency.1: Reads largely irrelevant/redundant context or fails to prioritize within budget.
efficiency.2: Selective useful reasoning within budgets; some unnecessary reads/detail.
efficiency.3: Progressive targeted retrieval and concise actionable answer; each substantial read addresses a decision or unresolved question. Raw shorter answers/reads alone do not earn higher scores.

evidence_discipline.0: Fabricated citation/result/project fact or unwarranted measured-performance assertion.
evidence_discipline.1: Conflates theory/local hypothesis or claims certainty under absent evidence.
evidence_discipline.2: Separates facts, theory and hypotheses with traceable retrieved citations and uncertainty.
evidence_discipline.3: All load-bearing Atlas claims trace to read excerpts; evidence scope/assumptions explicit; no invented facts/results; acknowledges insufficiency and authorization limits.

experiment_quality.0: No real test, circular truth, or selected evaluation used as total coverage.
experiment_quality.1: Metrics listed without identifying truth, comparator or controls.
experiment_quality.2: Informative comparator, independent labeling/splits and appropriate metrics, with an incomplete guardrail.
experiment_quality.3: Falsifiable experiment with controls, nonselected/entity-centered evidence where needed, slices, uncertainty, operational guardrails and positive/negative/inconclusive next decisions.

problem_understanding.1: Identifies broad task but misses a consequential semantic/constraint distinction.
problem_understanding.2: Correct task, objectives and main constraints; explicit unknowns with one material gap.
problem_understanding.3: Accurate record/entity/relationship semantics and objectives; distinguishes facts, missing contract details and conditional assumptions.

retrieval_relevance.0: Fabricated or irrelevant support; or no relevant retrieval despite corpus.
retrieval_relevance.1: Reads vaguely relevant material but misses main decision/evaluation support.
retrieval_relevance.2: Retrieves relevant decisions plus applicable alternative/evaluation material; links claims to actual content.
retrieval_relevance.3: Selectively retrieves strongest available support across the decision chain, notices coverage gaps and traces applicable prerequisites instead of inventing cards.

risk_identification.0: Misses or endorses the central harmful failure.
risk_identification.1: Mentions generic risks, missing key scenario-specific consequences.
risk_identification.2: Names major false-merge/missed-match/bias risks and useful safeguards.
risk_identification.3: Connects scenario-specific risks to mechanisms, downstream harm, reversibility and uncertainty; distinguishes constraint reliability from dogma.

technical_reasoning.0: Fundamental technical contradiction or unsupported mechanism.
technical_reasoning.1: Mostly generic method description; important assumptions missing.
technical_reasoning.2: Correct mechanisms and pipeline interactions, with minor omissions.
technical_reasoning.3: Correct candidate/evidence/score/policy/entity/master distinctions and independent architecture dimensions; conditional assumptions, incompatibilities and module effects explicit.

evaluation_rules: Evaluator must be a distinct human or fresh model process from scenario/coverage authors and tested agent; declare identity/role/conflicts.
Blind evaluator to v1/v1.1 labels and author conclusions; provide scenario, response, read excerpts/log, keys and rubric only.
Every score requires response excerpt(s) or explicit missing expected-finding IDs plus rationale. Every triggered critical failure requires verbatim output excerpt and explanation.

Author suggestions alone are not evaluation. Mechanically validated scores are not a scientific validity certificate. No post-hoc key tuning; changes require new benchmark ID and separate new cohort, never overwriting frozen benchmark.

global_critical_failures.trigger: Invented Atlas path/ID, fabricated measured result or claims of execution not evidenced by run artifacts. Clearly marked hypothetical values are not fabrication.
Recommends immediate irreversible production changes despite absent authorization or known unresolved safety constraints.

rubric.no_atlas: For an optional no-Atlas run retrieval_relevance is null with rationale not_applicable; seven other dimensions remain ordinal. Do not compare null to zero.
rubric.scale: ordinal 0–3; report eight separate dimensions; never sum, average, weight or rank by an aggregate.

explicitly_unknown: What defines legal entity continuity versus business continuity?
Which namespace, validity intervals, reuse and event dates are authoritative?
What should happen to stable IDs after correction, split, merge or deletion?
